newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to fresh closing record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to fresh closing record.

text.p: French stocks, propelled by a stronger dollar which is expected to boost the French economy, rose on Wednesday to a fresh closing record.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.58 points, or 1.35 percent, at an all-time closing high of 2,442.46. The index also set an intra-day high of 2,450.34 points. The CAC-40 January futures contract rose 28 points to 2,4446.
Volume was a heavy nine billion francs.
"The dollar's fabulous," a trader said. "The bond market is holding up nicely. The money just keeps flowing in."
The dollar rose to 5.5453 francs on Wednesday, bringing its gains against the French currency to 10 percent over two months. Economists expect a stronger dollar to spur French exports and investment.
Dollar stocks were obvious winners. Shares in oil company Elf Aquitaine rose 3.68 percent to close at 535 francs, and Total shares rose 3.1 percent to 465 francs.
Bank BNP shares surged 9.24 percent to 213.90 francs after being added to broker Cheuvreux de Virieu's favoured list of shares.

Shares in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics tumbled 11.97 percent to 379.40 francs after the company reported a drop in fourth-quarter profit and said a recovery in global semiconductor demand may not occur until 1998.

Euro Disney shares jumped 6.28 percent to 11.00 francs on a rise in 1996/97 first-quarter sales to 1.13 billion francs from 1.01 billion. The company reiterated that 1997 remains a challenging year due to rising finance charges. It had sounded a similar note of caution in November.
